beats.caption: Look! I<v>'m walking</v> with the sheep!

say: I'm walking with the sheep. The sun is going down. Mia is describing what is happening right now. This is the present continuous.
In this lesson, you'll learn how to make it, when to use it, and when not to use it.

data.heading: When do we use it?
data.rule: Now · Around now · Temporary · Future plans
examples: She<v>'s reading</v> a map right now.
He<v>'s staying</v> with his grandma this week.
We<v>'re meeting</v> Ali tomorrow at five.

say: We use the present continuous for actions in progress.
Right now, at this moment: she's reading a map right now.
Around now, these days: I'm learning English this year.
Temporary situations: he's staying with his grandma this week.
And fixed future plans, with a time: we're meeting Ali tomorrow at five.
In all of them, the action is not finished. It's in progress.
Look at Mia. She's walking through the grass. The wind is blowing, and the sheep are eating.
beats.caption: She<v>'s walking</v>. The sheep <v>are eating</v>.

say: The form has two parts: am, is or are, plus the verb with i n g.
I am walking. In speaking: I'm walking.
She is walking. She's walking.
They are walking. They're walking.
Both parts are important. Don't forget am, is or are!
Spelling. Most verbs just add i n g: read, reading.
If the verb ends in a silent e, drop the e: make, making. Write, writing.
One short vowel and one consonant at the end? Double the consonant: run, running. Sit, sitting. Swim, swimming.
And i e becomes y: lie, lying. Die, dying.
But be careful: see, seeing. Play, playing. These just add i n g.
Oh no! Whiskers is jumping across the river. Mia is reaching out her hand. Is he going to make it?
beats.caption: Whiskers <v>is jumping</v>! Mia <v>is reaching</v> out.

say: For the negative, add not after am, is or are.
I'm not sleeping.
She isn't listening.
They aren't playing now.
Remember: we say I'm not. There is no amn't in English.

beats.caption: I<v>'m not sleeping</v>. I<v>'m watching</v> the sunset!

data.heading: Questions and short answers
pairs: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.

say: For questions, put am, is or are first.
Are you listening? Yes, I am. Or, no, I'm not.
Is it raining? No, it isn't.
What are you doing? I'm reading a map.
Where is she going? She's going home.
Some words often go with the present continuous.
Now. Right now. At the moment.
Today. This week. These days.
And look and listen, when we point at something happening: look! It's snowing. Listen! The baby is crying.

data.heading: Present simple or continuous?
rows: She walks to school every day.
He's working from home this week.

say: How is it different from the present simple?
The present simple is for habits: she walks to school every day. The continuous is for now: she's walking to school now.
I usually drink tea. But today, I'm drinking coffee.
He works in a bank, that's permanent. But he's working from home this week, that's temporary.
Some verbs describe states, not actions. We don't usually use them with i n g.
Like, love, want, need.
Know, understand, believe.
And have, when it means own. So: I understand, not I'm understanding. I want ice cream, not I'm wanting ice cream.
The most common mistakes.
I reading now. We need am: I'm reading now.
She is play football. Add i n g: she is playing football.
I am understanding you. Understand is a state verb: I understand you.
Are you go home? Are you going home?
He is siting there. Double the t: he is sitting there.

data.heading: Repeat after me
lines: She's reading a book right now.

repeat.text: She's reading a book right now.

say: Now say them with me. Listen, then repeat.
Let's watch a little story. What's happening? Listen for i n g.
Mia is crossing the river. The water is rushing over the stones. She's holding a long stick, and she's walking very slowly.
beats.caption: Mia <v>is crossing</v> the river. She<v>'s holding</v> a stick.

say: Now she's on the other side. Whiskers is purring, and Mia is smiling. They're hugging each other.
beats.caption: They<v>'re hugging</v>. Whiskers <v>is purring</v>.

data.heading: Your turn!
data.sub: Pause the video if you need more time

say: Quiz time! Five questions, five seconds each.

beats.say_answer: Is sleeping. It's happening right now.
Know. Know is a state verb, so no i n g.
Are. Are you listening to me?

data.heading: Remember
items: Actions in progress: now, around now

say: Let's remember. The present continuous is for actions in progress, now or around now, for temporary situations, and for fixed plans.
It's am, is or are, plus verb i n g, with careful spelling. Negatives with not, and questions with am, is or are first.
And no i n g with state verbs like know, like and want.
